1	# zoxide
2	
3	**zoxide** is a smarter cd command, inspired by z and autojump.
4	
5	It remembers which directories you use most frequently, so you can "jump" to them in just a few keystrokes.
6	
7	## What does zoxide do?
8	
9	zoxide keeps track of the directories you use most frequently, and uses a ranking algorithm to navigate to the best match.
10	
11	## Usage Examples
12	
13	```sh
14	z foo              # cd into highest ranked directory matching foo
15	z foo bar          # cd into highest ranked directory matching foo and bar
16	z foo /            # cd into a subdirectory starting with foo
17	
18	z ~/foo            # z also works like a regular cd command
19	z foo/             # cd into relative path
20	z ..               # cd one level up
21	z -                # cd into previous directory
22	
23	zi foo             # cd with interactive selection (using fzf)
24	
25	z foo<SPACE><TAB>  # show interactive completions (bash 4.4+/fish/zsh only)
26	```
27	
28	## Installation
29	
30	zoxide can be installed on Linux, macOS, Windows, BSD, and Android through various package managers.
31	
32	### Linux / WSL
33	
34	Install using your distribution's package manager or via:
35	
36	```sh
37	curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ajeetdsouza/zoxide/main/install.sh | sh
38	```
39	
40	Available in package repositories for:
41	- Alpine Linux 3.13+: `apk add zoxide`
42	- Arch Linux: `pacman -S zoxide`
43	- Fedora 32+: `dnf install zoxide`
44	- Gentoo: `emerge app-shells/zoxide`
45	- openSUSE Tumbleweed: `zypper install zoxide`
46	- Void Linux: `xbps-install -S zoxide`
47	
48	And many others. See distribution documentation for details.
49	
50	### macOS
51	
52	Install using Homebrew or other package managers:
53	
54	```sh
55	brew install zoxide
56	```
57	
58	Or use the install script:
59	
60	```sh
61	curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ajeetdsouza/zoxide/main/install.sh | sh
62	```
63	
64	### Windows
65	
66	Install using winget:
67	
68	```sh
69	winget install ajeetdsouza.zoxide
70	```
71	
72	Or use alternative package managers:
73	- Chocolatey: `choco install zoxide`
74	- Scoop: `scoop install zoxide`
75	
76	### BSD
77	
78	Install using your distribution's package manager:
79	
80	- DragonFly BSD: `pkg install zoxide`
81	- FreeBSD: `pkg install zoxide`
82	- NetBSD: `pkgin install zoxide`
83	
84	Or use the install script:
85	
86	```sh
87	curl -sS https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ajeetdsouza/zoxide/main/install.sh | bash
88	```
89	
90	### Android
91	
92	Install using Termux:
93	
94	```sh
95	pkg install zoxide
96	```
97	
98	## Setup
99	
100	After installation, add zoxide to your shell configuration:
101	
102	### Bash
103	
104	Add to the end of `~/.bashrc`:
105	
106	```sh
107	eval "$(zoxide init bash)"
108	```
109	
110	### Zsh
111	
112	Add to the end of `~/.zshrc`:
113	
114	```sh
115	eval "$(zoxide init zsh)"
116	```
117	
118	For completions to work, this must be added after `compinit` is called.
119	
120	### Fish
121	
122	Add to the end of `~/.config/fish/config.fish`:
123	
124	```sh
125	zoxide init fish | source
126	```
127	
128	### PowerShell
129	
130	Add to the end of your PowerShell profile (find it by running `echo $profile`):
131	
132	```powershell
133	Invoke-Expression (& { (zoxide init powershell | Out-String) })
134	```
135	
136	### Elvish
137	
138	Add to the end of `~/.elvish/rc.elv`:
139	
140	```sh
141	eval (zoxide init elvish | slurp)
142	```
143	
144	(Requires elvish v0.18.0+)
145	
146	### Nushell
147	
148	Add to the end of your env file (find it by running `$nu.env-path`):
149	
150	```sh
151	zoxide init nushell | save -f ~/.zoxide.nu
152	```
153	
154	Add to the end of your config file (find it by running `$nu.config-path`):
155	
156	```sh
157	source ~/.zoxide.nu
158	```
159	
160	(Requires Nushell v0.89.0+)
161	
162	### Other shells
163	
164	For other POSIX-compatible shells, add to your config file:
165	
166	```sh
167	eval "$(zoxide init posix --hook prompt)"
168	```
169	
170	## Configuration
171	
172	### Command Flags
173	
174	When running `zoxide init`, the following flags are available:
175	
176	- `--cmd`: Changes the prefix of the `z` and `zi` commands
177	  - Example: `--cmd j` changes commands to `j` and `ji`
178	  - Example: `--cmd cd` replaces the `cd` command
179	
180	- `--hook <HOOK>`: Changes how often zoxide increments a directory's score
181	  - `none`: Never
182	  - `prompt`: At every shell prompt
183	  - `pwd` (default): Whenever the directory is changed
184	
185	- `--no-cmd`: Prevents zoxide from defining `z` and `zi` commands
186	  - Functions remain available as `__zoxide_z` and `__zoxide_zi`
187	
188	### Environment Variables
189	
190	Environment variables can be set before calling `zoxide init` to configure behavior:
191	
192	#### `_ZO_DATA_DIR`
193	
194	Specifies the directory where the database is stored.
195	
196	Default values:
197	- **Linux / BSD**: `$XDG_DATA_HOME` or `$HOME/.local/share`
198	- **macOS**: `$HOME/Library/Application Support`
199	- **Windows**: `%LOCALAPPDATA%`
200	
201	#### `_ZO_ECHO`
202	
203	When set to 1, `z` will print the matched directory before navigating to it.
204	
205	#### `_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS`
206	
207	Excludes specified directories from the database.
208	
209	Provided as a list of globs separated by OS-specific characters:
210	- **Linux / macOS / BSD**: `:` (colon), e.g., `$HOME:$HOME/private/*`
211	- **Windows**: `;` (semicolon), e.g., `$HOME;$HOME/private/*`
212	
213	Default: `$HOME`
214	
215	#### `_ZO_FZF_OPTS`
216	
217	Custom options to pass to fzf during interactive selection.
218	
219	#### `_ZO_MAXAGE`
220	
221	Configures the aging algorithm, which limits the maximum number of entries in the database.
222	
223	Default: 10000
224	
225	#### `_ZO_RESOLVE_SYMLINKS`
226	
227	When set to 1, `z` will resolve symlinks before adding directories to the database.
228	
229	## Subcommands
230	
231	- `zoxide add`: Add a new directory to the database, or increment its rank
232	- `zoxide import`: Import entries from another application
233	- `zoxide init`: Generate shell configuration
234	- `zoxide query`: Search for a directory in the database
235	- `zoxide remove`: Remove a directory from the database
236	
237	## Importing Data
238	
239	If you currently use autojump, fasd, z, z.lua, zsh-z, or ZLocation, you can import your data:
240	
241	```sh
242	zoxide import --from=autojump "/path/to/autojump/db"
243	zoxide import --from=z "/path/to/z/db"
244	```
245	
246	## Third-party Integrations
247	
248	zoxide integrates with many applications:
249	
250	- **File managers**: felix, joshuto, lf, nnn, ranger, rfm, xplr, yazi
251	- **Editors**: emacs, vim, neovim
252	- **Launchers**: alfred (macOS), raycast (macOS)
253	- **Shell enhancements**: clink (Windows), zsh-autocomplete
254	- **Terminal multiplexers**: tmux integrations (sesh, tmux-session-wizard, tmux-sessionx, zesh)
255	- **Other tools**: aerc, telescope.nvim, xxh, zabb
256	
257	## How It Works
258	
259	zoxide tracks directory usage and assigns each directory a score. When you run `z`, it matches your query against the database and navigates to the best match based on:
260	
261	- How frequently you visit the directory
262	- How recently you visited it
263	- How well the query matches the directory path
264	
265	The matching algorithm supports:
266	- Multiple keywords: `z foo bar` matches directories containing both "foo" and "bar"
267	- Fuzzy matching: Keywords can match anywhere in the path
268	- Prefix matching: Adding `/` restricts matching to directory prefixes
269	
270	## Requirements
271	
272	- For interactive selection (`zi`): fzf v0.51.0 or later (optional)
273	
274	## License
275	
276	See LICENSE file for details.
